sphere_sdf — 3D sdf_csg op

• Data kinds: coordgrid → sdf

• Call: import fullseye as fs; fs.ledger.sphere_sdf(grid, center, R) (to call the implementation directly, import sdf_ops; sdf_ops.sphere_sdf(grid, center, R); from the registry, ops3d.get("sphere_sdf"))

Usage

The signed distance field of a sphere: |p − center| − R (negative inside, positive outside).

grid is a coordinate array whose last axis is 3, (..., 3) (output of grid_coords or an (N,3) point cloud). center has length 3, R>=0 is the radius. The returned shape is grid.shape[:-1]. An exact SDF (gradient norm 1). sdf_offset(sphere_sdf(g,c,R), r) == sphere_sdf(g,c,R+r).

Raises ValueError for R<0 or malformed grid/center.

Computation: np.linalg.norm(grid - center, axis=-1) - R. Coordinate units carry over directly as distance units (pass the world coordinates of grid_coords and you get world units). The component order of the coordinates is the order of the last axis of grid ((x, y, z) for grid_coords), and center uses the same order.

Arguments and validation (ValueError):

• grid: float array whose last axis is 3, (..., 3) (1-D (3,) is also allowed; 0-D or a last axis other than 3 is rejected).

• center: 3 elements (numpy's ValueError if reshape(3) fails).

• R: a scalar that float() accepts. Passing a rotation matrix or the like also gives ValueError (this argument is a radius, not a pose). R < 0 is rejected; R = 0 gives the distance field from the centre itself.

Returns: float64 of grid.shape[:-1] ((nx, ny, nz) for the output of grid_coords). -R at the centre, 0 on the surface, positive outside.

Usage: grid with grid_coords → sphere_sdf / box_sdf → CSG with sdf_union / sdf_subtract → marching cubes with <= 0 as occupied (pass -sdf to voxel_to_mesh for the isosurface equivalent to iso=0).
